title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We measure how inserting a deterministic network verifier into a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) loop affects verifier-detected safety violations for LLM-produced device-configuration proposals. In a preregistered paired design (N = 500 intent→configuration tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters) we compared: (1) baseline — a single shared LLM proposal produced once per task, and (2) guarded — the identical shared proposal validated by a deterministic netops verifier and subjected to up to one automated repair iteration when the verifier flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). The preregistered exact McNemar two-sided test was implemented as an exact binomial on discordant pairs (n = n10 + n01); with n = 1 and n10 = 1 the archived two-sided p = 1.00 under that convention. Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; the marginal verifier+repair effect on the pass-rate metric is therefore small, though the verifier corrected one concrete baseline failure. All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are rapidly being applied to NetOps tasks including operator-intent translation to device configuration, multi-step change planning, and automated repair. System reports and surveys emphasize that operational safety depends heavily on surrounding engineering such as deterministic validators, sandbox replay, canarying, and rollback mechanisms [Beckett et al., 2017; Wei et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. The generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) operational pattern—LLM candidate generation followed by deterministic verification and automated or human-in-the-loop repair—has been proposed across structured-generation domains to improve correctness. However, controlled measurements that isolate the verifier’s marginal contribution while holding the LLM proposal fixed are scarce. Practitioners face a concrete operational question: when an LLM already produces high-quality candidates on verifier-modeled properties, how much incremental safety does an inserted verifier plus a modest automated-repair budget provide on a verifier-scoped pass/fail metric? We answer this question with a preregistered paired experiment that intentionally isolates verifier+repair impact under deterministic semantics.
sections.related_work: Deterministic/formal verification methods for network configurations (header-space analysis, route-model verifiers, Batfish-style analyzers) provide machine-checkable properties such as reachability, isolation, and update-atomicity and are established in NetOps verification literature [Beckett et al., 2017]. Recent NetOps/AIOps research integrates LLMs for intent parsing and configuration generation while advocating guardrails for operational reliability (e.g., INTA, Confucius, and other agentic NetOps frameworks) [INTA, 2025; Wang et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. Generate–verify–repair (or generate–critic) architectures have been proposed to reduce incorrect or unsafe structured outputs [PoeTone; INTA]. Separate literature documents LLM failure modes (hallucination, overconfidence, integration errors) and recommends verification or human oversight as mitigations [Owen, 2026; DeepSeek-AI, 2025]. Where our study differs is a preregistered, artifact-backed, within-task paired ablation that keeps the LLM’s initial output identical across arms (shared_initial_candidate semantics) and therefore isolates the marginal effect of deterministic verification plus a single automated repair iteration.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory plan. We preregistered study_id cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026, freezing research questions, stratification, inclusion/exclusion rules, estimands, analysis executor, multiplicity plan, retry policy, and stopping rule before observing outcomes. The primary confirmatory hypothesis: an LLM paired with a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair iteration will produce a lower verifier-detected safety-violation rate than the same LLM producing a single proposal without verifier feedback (paired within-task). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where success == verifier reports zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations. The preregistration and full support artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle (preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the execution manifest).

Task generation and stratification. A deterministic synthetic corpus of 500 intent→configuration tasks was produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 using the preregistered seeds. Tasks were stratified into three clusters as preregistered: VLAN-change = 167 tasks, ACL-change = 167 tasks, static-route-change = 166 tasks. Execution artifacts (execution/task_manifest.jsonl) confirm that the realized per-cluster counts match the preregistered allocation (no confirmatory exclusions occurred) and that complete_pair_count = 500. The generator constrained tasks to features modeled by the verifier (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}) so that pass/fail is defined relative to verifier coverage.

Generation semantics, model, and verifier. To isolate marginal verifier effect we used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (independent_condition_generation = false). For each task the pipeline produced one shared LLM proposal; this identical candidate served as the baseline output and was also validated by the guarded arm. The guarded path invoked an automated single-repair call only if the deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) reported a preregistered high/medium-severity violation on the shared candidate. Requested LLM = gpt-5-mini called through the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter; model_configuration.json in the archive records generation parameters. The guarded arm permitted at most one automated repair iteration per the preregistration.

Statistical test implementation. The preregistered confirmatory test was an exact McNemar two-sided test on paired binary outcomes. Our archived executor implements that two-sided test via an exact binomial on discordant pairs: let n = n10 + n01 (discordant pairs), and let X = n10 (pairs where guarded passes but baseline fails, under the executor’s discordant-ordering convention). Under the null that discordant outcomes are equally likely, X ∼ Binomial(n, 0.5). The two-sided p-value is computed as p_two-sided = 2 * min{P(X ≤ x), P(X ≥ x)} (with truncation at 1.0). For the observed counts (n = 1, x = 1) this yields the archived p = 1.00. We report this exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs result and complement it with a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (B = 10,000, seed = 1729) for the absolute difference; resampling preserves pairing (draw 500 pairs with replacement per resample). The analysis implementation and parameters are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes. The run completed with complete_pair_count = 500 and model_calls_used = 501 (shared_initial_generation = 500; repair-stage calls observed = 1). Aggregated per-condition counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded_success_rate = 1.000). Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002.

Inference and uncertainty. Using the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs implementation gives two-sided p = 1.00 for the observed discordant counts (n = 1, n10 = 1) because small n produces non-intuitive exact p-values under that convention; the archived computation and code path are available for deterministic re-inspection. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute difference is [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). These results indicate a small point-estimate improvement but substantial inferential uncertainty driven by a near-ceiling baseline.

Repair activity and the discordant pair. Observed repair-stage provider calls = 1 and that single repair produced the sole discordant outcome (n10 = 1): the guarded arm converted one baseline-detected violation to a verified pass. Deterministic run-level artifacts confirm exactly one such discordant episode. The full validator_trace and repair-stage provider traces for that episode are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl and in the provider-call traces; the manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json confirm repair-stage calls = 1. To preserve archival provenance and avoid disclosure of raw provider traces in the manuscript, readers can deterministically locate the discordant episode by filtering execution/raw_results.jsonl for entries where baseline scoring indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) and guarded scoring indicates pass == 1; because exactly one such entry exists this lookup returns that single episode and its validator_trace and repair traces. The archived validator_trace for the episode records a verifier-detected preregistered violation and that the repair-stage call produced a repaired candidate which the verifier then accepted; full per-task diagnostics and repair prompts/responses are available in the evidence bundle.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the constrained experimental regime—single requested LLM (gpt-5-mini), shared_initial_candidate semantics, deterministic verifier modeling a limited feature set (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}), and at most one automated repair iteration—the LLM produced near-ceiling correct proposals and the marginal measured pass-rate benefit of adding the verifier was small (0.002). This conditional result documents a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality (on verifier-scoped properties) is very high, a modest verifier+repair budget may yield negligible measurable pass-rate gains on a composite pass/fail metric, although the verifier can still correct rare concrete failures (as observed here).

Design-choice implications. The shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolate verifier+repair effect conditional on identical proposals and match deployment semantics that preserve an original human-reviewed proposal for repair rather than regeneration. This design does not evaluate alternative choices such as verifier-guided regeneration, multiple repair iterations, or cost-weighted objectives; those alternatives could yield larger effect sizes and require separate preregistered measurements.

Threats to validity. Internal validity is supported by preregistration, deterministic task seeds, and automated replacement/contamination checks; no manual adjudication occurred. Construct validity is limited by verifier coverage: the pass==no high/medium-severity violations outcome is defined relative to the verifier’s modeled properties and severity mapping archived in the validator-spec artifacts; properties outside that modeled set are not measured. External validity is limited by single-model testing (requested gpt-5-mini), a synthetic task corpus, and constrained feature scope; we do not claim cross-vendor or multi-model generality.

Statistical nuance. The archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention implemented by the analysis executor and the small discordant count; users should interpret this p-value in the context of the extreme ceiling effect. The paired-bootstrap CI provides additional quantification of uncertainty around the small absolute improvement.
sections.conclusion: We performed a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment (N = 500) that isolated verifier+single-repair effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The LLM produced near-ceiling verifier-scoped proposals (baseline 499/500; guarded 500/500), yielding an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]; archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the run’s exact-binomial convention). This conditional measurement illustrates a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality is very high for the verifier-modeled properties and the verifier’s coverage is limited, the measurable marginal pass-rate benefit of a modest verifier+repair budget can be negligible on a composite pass/fail metric, though the verifier can still correct rare concrete failures. Practitioners should (1) measure baseline proposal error prevalence on representative workloads before allocating repair budgets, (2) align verifier coverage with operator-critical constraints, and (3) select generation/repair semantics to match deployment priorities. All preregistration, code, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call logs, execution manifests, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection.

limitations: Synthetic, deterministic task corpus limited to features modeled by the deterministic validator; task payloads constrained to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}. Results do not generalize to unconstrained production intents, cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or protocol semantics outside the verifier scope.
Single requested model family (gpt-5-mini requested) and a single validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — no claim of multi-model or cross-validator generality is made.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets or iterative regeneration strategies could change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) created a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention and the small discordant count.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl in the evidence bundle. To inspect it deterministically: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair entries where the baseline scoring outcome indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) while the guarded scoring outcome indicates pass == 1; because only one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this lookup returns the single episode and its provider-call traces. The validator violation-code→severity mapping is archived in the execution manifest and validator-spec artifacts in the bundle.
